title: OpenAI ChatCompletions compatibility facade: request & response mapping + streaming semantics
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Ship a compatibility facade that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions v1 request shapes and returns responses that match OpenAI semantics while routing through Redwood's native runtime. The facade should: (1) map incoming 'messages' and role semantics into Redwood's internal prompt representation; (2) translate function definitions and function_call behavior into our tool-calling primitives; (3) stream responses using OpenAI-style delta chunks (including function_call deltas) and reconcile with Redwood streaming frames; (4) produce response objects with choices[], finish_reason, index, and usage fields compatible with OpenAI clients. This enables existing customers and third-party integrations expecting the OpenAI wire format to migrate to Redwood with minimal client changes.
acceptance_criteria: Facade endpoint POST /v1/chat/completions accepts OpenAI-style body and returns 200 with choices array on non-streaming calls
Streaming mode returns SSE/HTTP chunks following OpenAI delta format for both content and function_call fragments
Function calling: when a model triggers a function_call, the facade emits a single choice with a function_call object (name + arguments string) matching OpenAI ordering and content encoding
Structured output: when a schema constraint is provided via 'json_schema' or function signatures, facade surfaces validation errors or structured fields in a way OpenAI clients expect
Usage fields (prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens) are populated using Redwood's token accounting and appear in the response.
decisions: Map OpenAI 'system/user/assistant' roles -> Redwood's role tokens with an explicit role header; do not drop role metadata
Stream format: reuse Redwood streaming internals but synthesize OpenAI 'delta' envelopes. Each Redwood stream chunk will be transformed into one or more OpenAI delta events if needed

Function arguments will be accumulated as a contiguous string in the choice.function_call.arguments field to match OpenAI; we will also emit granular function_call delta events during streaming for better UX
Errors: Translate Redwood runtime errors to OpenAI-like error payloads with 'type' and 'message' fields; do not expose internal traces by default
We will not attempt byte-perfect usage token accounting for the first rollout; approximate totals will be returned with a 'deprecated' annotation in docs until refined.
implementation_notes: Add a new package api-compat/openai-chatfacade with routing for /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings shim routes
Create a request normalizer: convert OpenAI request body -> internal RequestContext (messages, functions, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences)
Create a response formatter: internal Response -> OpenAI response shape with choices[], usage, and top-level id/model fields
Streaming adapter will buffer Redwood token deltas and emit OpenAI delta slices; implement backpressure-aware batching to avoid increased latency
Integrate with function-calling execution: when a function is invoked, convert returned structured output to a function_call message and ensure correct ordering in choices array
Add feature flag 'compat.openai_chat_v1' behind which the facade runs for canary rollout
Add detailed logging mapping IDs for traceability (request_id, facade_id, model_request_id) without leaking PII or prompt content in prod logs
test_plan: Unit tests: request normalizer and response formatter edge cases (empty messages, multi-function definitions, stop sequences)
Integration tests: end-to-end request -> model -> function invocation -> final response for both streaming and non-streaming
Contract tests: run OpenAI SDK language clients (python/js) against the facade with a known test harness and ensure shape compatibility
Load test: synthetic workload that mirrors existing OpenAI traffic patterns ensuring latency SLOs under 75th/95th percentile
Security test: ensure API keys and auth headers follow Redwood auth rules and rate-limits are honored
comments: 2025-06-19 - Marisol Vega: Spike complete. Confirmed primary differences: streaming delta granularity and function_call encoding. Prototype available in /tmp/spike-openai-facade.tar.gz

2025-06-22 - Ethan Park: Reviewed prototype. Two concerns: token accounting gap & behavior when user supplies both 'functions' and 'function_call': we should mirror OpenAI's precedence rules. Adding to decisions.
2025-06-26 - Aisha Fernando (PM): High priority for customers migrating from OpenAI. Recommend exposing a 'compatibility_mode' response header during canary to collect client compatibility metrics.
2025-06-30 - Design review (DES-312): Suggested response examples for edge cases (multi-choice streaming, aborted function calls). Design artifacts linked.
2025-07-02 - Ethan Park: Implemented basic streaming adapter and added feature flag. PR opened: api-compat #17. Requesting review from infra for SSE connection behavior.
notes: Make facade idempotent for retry semantics. Ensure we document any incompatibilities (e.g., minor differences in token counts, ordering of assistant/system messages). After canary, we will produce a migration guide for clients.
